title: Naperville Home Energy Rebates 2026: City Electric and Nicor Gas
desc: Naperville home energy rebates in 2026: the city's own electric utility pays up to $1,800 for a heat pump and $75 for a thermostat, Nicor Gas pays for furnaces and insulation. ComEd does not apply.
lead: Naperville homeowners have a different set of rebates from most of the Chicago area, because the city runs its own electric utility. The City of Naperville pays up to $1,800 for a heat pump and $75 for a smart thermostat. Its attic insulation and window money is used up for 2026. Nicor Gas pays for gas furnaces, boilers, insulation and air sealing. ComEd rebates are not for Naperville customers. We confirmed these on October 6, 2026.

sections:
The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 survey counts 57,135 homes in Naperville and 54,847 lived in year-round. Owners are 74.8% of households and renters 25.2%. Detached houses are 62.8% of homes, attached houses 12.2% and buildings of two to four homes 4.6%.

Only 25.8% of homes were built before 1980, and 23.1% since 2000. Utility gas heats 86.1% of homes and electricity 11.9%.

Your electric rebates come from the city. Your gas rebates come from Nicor Gas. The two do not share forms or deadlines. The city gives a one-time credit on your electric bill. Nicor pays a prepaid card or a check six to eight weeks after you apply, and wants the application within 90 days of the work.
Why ComEd pages do not apply
Many web pages about Illinois rebates mention ComEd. In Naperville those do not apply, since ComEd does not deliver your electricity. Read our Naperville Electric page for the city's offers.

If you want a heat pump, check that city funds remain, then install and apply within 120 days. If you want attic insulation or windows, the city money is closed now, so decide whether to use Nicor's rebate this year or to wait and ask the city about 2027. Nicor's attic rebate pays $400. The city's was $1 a square foot up to $2,500 in 2026.
Renters, owners and what is missing

One Naperville household in four rents. The city's heat pump and thermostat pages say owners or renters can apply, though a tenant still needs the landlord's permission to put in a heat pump. We found no Naperville rebate for a home battery, an electric car charger or a heat pump water heater on an official page, so we list none. The federal credits that once covered those ended after 2025.
Illinois Shines credit payments are the state's main solar incentive, but we did not read which pricing group applies at a Naperville address. Ask an approved vendor. See our Illinois solar guide.
claim_heading: How to use these rebates in Naperville
claim_steps: Check that your electric bill comes from the city and your gas from Nicor Gas.
Call the city at 630-305-5357 to ask what funds remain.
Choose the heat pump or thermostat and keep every receipt.
Apply to the city within 120 days and to Nicor within 90 days.
If your income is low, apply for free state weatherization.

faq: Who is my electric company in Naperville?
The City of Naperville's own electric utility.
Can I use ComEd rebates in Naperville?
No. ComEd's rebates are for ComEd customers.
What is the biggest Naperville rebate?
The city's $1,800 heat pump rebate when you do not keep a gas furnace for backup.
Why are attic and window rebates closed?
The city says it awarded the full $280,000 budget as of June 26, 2026.
